ai.literal: As proper conduct let consider a person his in heart envy without nature.
ai.translation: Let a person consider the nature of being without envy in his heart as his proper conduct.
ai.modern: ஒருவன் தன் நெஞ்சத்தில் பொறாமை இல்லாத குணத்தையே தனக்கான சிறந்த ஒழுக்கமாகக் கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the core of good conduct as the absence of envy. The word 'ஒழுக்காறு' refers to the path of proper behavior or morality. The poet advises that a person should actively adopt a nature ('இயல்பு') free from envy ('அழுக்காறு') in their heart. True morality is thus presented not just as outward actions, but as a pure internal state of mind.

ai.literal: Among excellent gains, an equal thing to that is not, with anyone, the absence of envy if obtained.
ai.translation: If one can achieve the absence of envy towards anyone, there is no equal to that among excellent gains.
ai.modern: யாரிடத்திலும் பொறாமை இல்லாத தன்மையை ஒருவர் பெற்றால், அவர் அடையும் சிறந்த பேறுகளில் அதற்கு இணையானது வேறு எதுவும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme value of a mind free from envy. The phrase 'அழுக்காற்றின் அன்மை' means the complete absence of envy towards anyone ('யார் மாட்டும்'). The poet declares that if a person can attain this state, there is no other excellent gain ('விழுப்பேறு') that can equal it. Because envy destroys one's own peace and character, being entirely free from it is presented as the highest possible achievement.

ai.literal: Virtue [and] prosperity he-desires-not he-who-is-called, another's prosperity not-cherishing he-who-envies.
ai.translation: He who envies another's prosperity instead of rejoicing in it is known as one who desires neither virtue nor his own prosperity.
ai.modern: மற்றவருடைய வளர்ச்சியைக் கண்டு மகிழாமல் பொறாமைப்படுபவன், தனக்கு அறமும் செல்வமும் வேண்டாம் என்று நினைப்பவன் ஆவான்.
ai.explanation: The word 'ஆக்கம்' (ākkam) can mean wealth, creation, or general prosperity; here it refers to prosperity or growth, applying both to oneself and to others. This couplet defines the true nature of an envious person. By refusing to cherish the prosperity of others ('பிறன் ஆக்கம் பேணாது') and choosing to envy them instead ('அழுக்கறுப்பான்'), a person actively rejects their own well-being. The text states that such a person is known as one who does not desire virtue and their own prosperity ('அறன் ஆக்கம் வேண்டாதான்'). Envy is thus framed not just as a harm to others, but as a self-destructive rejection of one's own moral and material growth.

ai.literal: Out of envy evil deeds they will not do, by the path of fault misery happening having known.
ai.translation: Knowing that misery will come from the path of fault, they will not commit evil deeds out of envy.
ai.modern: பொறாமையினால் தீய செயல்களைச் செய்ய மாட்டார்கள், அந்தத் தவறான வழியினால் தமக்குத் துன்பம் வரும் என்பதை அறிந்து.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains why wise people avoid acting out of envy. They understand that envy is a flawed path that inevitably brings misery to themselves. Knowing the harm that follows such an error, they refrain from doing evil deeds driven by jealousy.

ai.literal: Envy to those who possess, that is enough; enemies even if failing, ruin that which yields.
ai.translation: For those who harbor envy, that alone is enough to destroy them. Even if they have no enemies to cause them harm, their own envy will bring about their ruin.
ai.modern: பொறாமை குணம் கொண்டவர்களுக்கு அவர்களை அழிக்க அந்தப் பொறாமையே போதும். அவர்களுக்குத் தீங்கு செய்ய பகைவர்கள் தவறினாலும், அந்தப் பொறாமையே அவர்களுக்குக் கேட்டைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the self-destructive nature of envy. The word 'அழுக்காறு' refers to jealousy or envy, and the poet states that possessing it is sufficient to bring about one's own downfall. Even if external enemies fail to cause harm, the internal flaw of envy will inevitably yield ruin.

ai.literal: that which is given - envy - he who harbours - relatives - clothing even - food even - without - will perish
ai.translation: The family of one who envies what is given to others will perish, left without even food and clothing.
ai.modern: பிறருக்குக் கொடுக்கப்படுவதைக் கண்டு பொறாமைப்படுபவனின் சுற்றத்தார், உடுப்பதற்கு உடையும் உண்பதற்கு உணவும் இல்லாமல் அழிந்து போவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns of the destructive consequences of envy. If a person feels jealous when seeing others receive gifts or charity, that envy will ruin not just him but his entire family. The lengthened words 'உடுப்பதூஉம்' (even clothing) and 'உண்பதூஉம்' (even food) use a poetic device (aḷapeṭai) to emphasize the absolute destitution that will befall them, leaving them without the most basic necessities of life.

ai.literal: Having envied, him who possesses envy, the goddess of wealth, her elder sister, having shown, will leave.
ai.translation: The goddess of wealth will introduce the envious man to her elder sister, the goddess of misfortune, and then abandon him.
ai.modern: பொறாமை குணம் கொண்டவனைச் செல்வமகள் தன் தமக்கையான வறுமையிடம் காட்டிவிட்டு, அவனை விட்டு விலகிப் போய்விடுவாள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet personifies prosperity and adversity as two sisters. 'Ceyyavaḷ' (the red or prosperous woman) represents prosperity, while her elder sister 'Tavvai' represents misfortune. The poet warns that if a person harbors envy ('aḻukkāṟu'), prosperity will refuse to stay with him. Instead, she will introduce him to her elder sister, adversity, and abandon him to a life of ruin.

ai.literal: Envy called one sinner, wealth having destroyed, evil place having driven will leave.
ai.translation: The sinner called envy will destroy a person's wealth and drive them into a place of evil.
ai.modern: அழுக்காறு என்று சொல்லப்படும் பாவி, ஒருவனுடைய செல்வத்தை அழித்து, அவனைத் துன்பமான இடத்தில் கொண்டுபோய் தள்ளிவிடும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet personifies envy as an unparalleled sinner ('பாவி'). This destructive force acts directly against the envious person by first destroying their present wealth and prosperity ('திருச் செற்று'). Finally, it drives them into a place of evil or suffering ('தீயுழி'). The word 'தீ' can mean fire or evil, but here it describes a state of ruin where envy ultimately leads its host.

ai.literal: Envious heart-he-of prosperity-and, upright-man-of ruin-and, to-ponder will-be.
ai.translation: The prosperity of a man with an envious heart, and the ruin of an upright man, are things to be deeply pondered.
ai.modern: பொறாமை கொண்ட மனம் உடையவனின் செல்வமும், நேர்மையான மனம் உடையவனின் வறுமையும் சான்றோரால் ஆராய்ந்து பார்க்கப்படும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts two unexpected situations: an envious person gaining wealth ('ஆக்கம்') and a righteous person facing ruin ('கேடு'). The word 'அவ்விய' means crooked or envious, fitting the chapter's theme of not envying, while 'செவ்வியான்' denotes someone who is straight and upright. The phrase 'நினைக்கப் படும்' indicates that these outcomes will be deeply pondered, as they seem to contradict the natural order of justice. The text implies that such unnatural states are anomalies that provoke thought about their true causes and ultimate consequences.

ai.literal: Having envied, even those who prospered are not; those who do not have that, even those who departed from prosperity are not.
ai.translation: No one has ever achieved greatness through envy. Likewise, no one free from envy has ever fallen from prosperity.
ai.modern: பொறாமை கொண்டு வாழ்வில் உயர்ந்தவர்களும் இல்லை; பொறாமை இல்லாதவர்கள் செல்வத்திலிருந்து நீங்கித் தாழ்ந்தவர்களும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: The couplet states a clear rule about the consequences of envy. It says that those who harbor envy never achieve true greatness or prosperity. Conversely, those who are completely free from that flaw never lose their prosperity. The word 'அகன்றார்' means those who have expanded or grown great, while 'தீர்ந்தார்' means those who have fallen away or separated from their wealth.
